stimulus.value: Archival preservation in historic libraries relies on microclimate regulation. Fluctuations in relative humidity accelerate cellulose hydrolysis, destabilizing paper structures.

questions.stem: Which factor most directly accelerates cellulose degradation in historic paper?
questions.solution: The stimulus directly states that relative humidity fluctuations accelerate cellulose hydrolysis.

questions.stem: Select the option that best summarizes the principle of steady iterative preparation without excessive pressure.

options.text: Continuous, deliberate practice with structured pacing builds composure and reliable decision-making.
Intensive cramming during final stages guarantees superior examination recall.
Attempting every single problem regardless of complexity optimizes percentile return.
Intuitive guessing provides superior time dividends compared to structured filtering.

questions.solution: Option A captures the core concept of deliberate pacing and composure without exaggerated claims.

questions.stem: Arrange the sentences in logical sequence: 1. This feedback loop guides revision. 2. A baseline assessment records decision times. 3. Insights highlight operational bottlenecks. 4. Next, pattern summaries are generated.
questions.solution: Sequence 2 -> 4 -> 3 -> 1 flows naturally from assessment to patterns, insights, and guiding revision.

questions.stem: An urban transport analyst observes that expanding bus lanes increased transit throughput while personal vehicular commute times remained steady. Which proposition supports this finding?

options.text: Commuters shifted from single-occupancy vehicles to rapid bus routes, offsetting corridor congestion.
Bus fuel consumption increased proportionately with frequency.
Pedestrian footpaths were widened simultaneously along peripheral routes.
Automated toll gates were installed exclusively outside city perimeters.

questions.solution: A modal shift to rapid transit explains higher throughput alongside stable private vehicle times.

questions.stem: Four analysts (A, B, C, D) sit in a straight row facing North. A sits at the westernmost end. C sits between B and D. Who sits adjacent to A?

options.text: Cannot be determined without additional constraints

questions.solution: If A is at pos 1, C is between B and D so B and D occupy positions 2 and 4 with C at 3. Thus B or D is adjacent. With order A-B-C-D, B sits next to A.

stimulus.value: Quarterly solar generation (GWh): Q1: 120, Q2: 150, Q3: 180, Q4: 150.

questions.stem: What is the average quarterly generation across the year?
In a cohort of 50 scholars, 30 read microeconomics, 25 read econometrics, and 10 read both. How many read neither subject?
questions.solution: Total reading at least one = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. Neither = 50 - 45 = 5.

questions.stem: In a single-elimination tournament with 16 seeded competitors, how many total matches are played to determine the sole champion?
questions.solution: In any single-elimination tournament, each match eliminates exactly one participant. Thus 16 - 1 = 15 matches.

questions.stem: A merchant marks an item 25% above cost and offers a 10% cash discount. What is the net profit percentage?
questions.solution: Let cost be 100. Marked price = 125. Selling price after 10% discount = 125 - 12.5 = 112.5. Profit = 12.5%.

questions.stem: If x + (1 / x) = 3 for x > 0, what is the value of x^2 + (1 / x^2)?
A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm and one leg 5 cm. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.solution: Second leg = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(169 - 25) = 12 cm. Area = (1/2) * 5 * 12 = 30 cm².

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 2^50 is divided by 7?
A courier travels 15 km at 10 km/h and another 15 km at 15 km/h. What is the average speed over the entire 30 km journey?
questions.solution: Total time = 15/10 + 15/15 = 1.5 + 1.0 = 2.5 hours. Average speed = 30 / 2.5 = 12 km/h.

questions.stem: If 2x + 3y = 12 and x - y = 1, what is the value of x + y?
questions.solution: From x = y + 1, substitute: 2(y + 1) + 3y = 12 => 5y + 2 = 12 => y = 2, x = 3? Wait: 2(3)+3(2)=12. Then x=3, y=2 gives x-y=1 and 2x+3y=12. So x+y = 5. (Let A be 5).

questions.stem: Inlet pipes A and B fill an empty storage tank in 6 hours and 9 hours respectively. Operating simultaneously, how many hours will they take to fill the tank?
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/9 = 5/18 per hour. Time = 18/5 = 3.6 hours.

questions.stem: The perimeter of a square is equal to the circumference of a circle. What is the ratio of the area of the circle to the area of the square?
questions.solution: 4s = 2πr => s = πr/2. Area circle / Area square = (πr^2) / (π^2 r^2 / 4) = 4 / π.

questions.stem: In how many distinct ways can 5 distinct reference manuals be arranged on a shelf such that two specified manuals are never placed next to each other?
questions.solution: Total arrangements = 5! = 120. Treating the pair as one block = 4! * 2! = 48. Not together = 120 - 48 = 72.

questions.stem: If 8 technicians complete a calibration run in 12 days, how many technicians working at the same pace are needed to complete it in 6 days?
questions.solution: Total work = 8 * 12 = 96 technician-days. For 6 days, 96 / 6 = 16 technicians.

questions.stem: What is the highest power of 5 that divides 100! without a remainder?
Find the minimum value attained by the quadratic function f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 13 across all real numbers x.
questions.solution: f(x) = (x - 3)^2 + 4. Since (x - 3)^2 >= 0, minimum value is 4 at x = 3.

questions.stem: Two concentric circular rings have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. What is the length of the chord of the larger ring that is tangent to the inner ring?
questions.solution: Half chord = sqrt(5^2 - 3^2) = sqrt(25 - 9) = 4 cm. Full chord = 2 * 4 = 8 cm.
